subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THREE FINDINGS. Findings 1 and 2 together are a CORRECTION AND EXTENSION of claim.law.cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base.20260831.v1; finding 3 is a methodological boundary on claim.law.address-pre-hoist-survives-every-address-spelling.20260831.v1.

FINDING 1 - WHEN THE TARGET REACHES SYMBOL B THROUGH SYMBOL A'S RELOCATION, A AND B ARE ONE DECLARED OBJECT. Diagnostic: the target materialises `lis rT,A@ha ; addi rHOME,rT,A@lo` once, then reaches data belonging to the NEXT split symbol B with the A->B distance FOLDED INTO THE LOAD/STORE DISPLACEMENT (`stw r3,1412(r4)`), with no relocation on the access itself. A compiler cannot fold a cross-object distance into a displacement, so this shape PROVES the two symbols were one declared object in the original source and the extractor split them - typically because some other function references B's address directly, which mints a second symbol at that offset. Here sSpeechNameBuf (.bss 0x8028B5D0, size 0x40, a sprintf scratch buffer) and sActiveTrackId (.bss 0x8028BA80, size 0x238) are exactly 0x4B0 apart, and AudioSetupBossStreams reaches every id at `sSpeechNameBuf + 0x4B0..0x6C4`. The cure is to declare ONE record spanning both and keep the FIRST symbol as the declared base, per claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity: here `typedef struct { char name[0x40]; u8 pad_40[0x470]; s32 activeTrack[45]; s32 boss[12][8]; } SpeechBlock;` with `SpeechBlock* speech = (SpeechBlock*)sSpeechNameBuf`. Note the layout falls out of the offsets with no guesswork: 0x4B0 + 45*4 = 0x564 is exactly where the row table starts, and the 0x20 row stride makes it [12][8]. Do NOT re-base to B - that emits a different relocation.

FINDING 2 - THE ALIAS THAT DEFEATS REMATERIALISATION DOES NOT HAVE TO BE SOURCE-DECLARED; THE CAST-POINTER-ARITHMETIC SPELLING MANUFACTURES IT INSIDE THE COMPILER. The parent law tells you to hold NO cached alias so MWCC rematerialises `add rX,rBase,rIdx` per access, and lists the aliases to remove as SOURCE constructs (`T* p = &arr[i];`, derived field pointers, handle aliases). This function had none of those and still hoisted, because the ACCESS SPELLING itself was enough: 15 accesses written as `*(s32*)(base + CONST + i * 4)` let MWCC reassociate to (base + i*4) + CONST, find `base + i*4` common across all 15, and park that synthesised value in one callee-saved GPR for the whole function - the compiler creates the cached alias the parent law only knew how to remove from source. Respelling every access as an array reference into a declared record (`speech->boss[n][idx]`, `speech->activeTrack[sel]`) restored the target's shape exactly: MWCC then CSEs ONLY the index shift (`slwi r29,r25,2` once) and rematerialises `add rX,r30,r29` before each access, folding the row constant into the store displacement. MEASURED: 18 target-only `add` appeared on our side, the opcode multiset went 22 tokens -> 1, and the instruction count went from 16 SHORT to exactly one LONG. So read the parent law's precondition as: hold no cached alias AND spell each access as an array/member reference into a declared record - raw offset arithmetic behind a cast is itself a cached alias. This makes the conversion simultaneously a de-fakematch win and a matching win, as the parent law's corollary predicts.

FINDING 3 - PROBING ONE SITE OF AN N-SITE CSE POPULATION MEASURES NOTHING, AND A NULL THERE MUST NOT BE GENERALISED. The prior pass on this function (attempt.sounds-evt-bossstreams-aligned-read-followup.20260831.v2) spent both its probes respelling a SINGLE access - two structurally distinct address spellings, both correctly measured byte-identical - and concluded from that null that the address-spelling axis was closed, citing claim.law.address-pre-hoist-survives-every-address-spelling. A single occurrence has no common subexpression to defeat, so the probe could not have moved anything whatever the spelling: the null was guaranteed by the experimental design, not by the compiler. The parent rematerialisation law already warns the conversion is ALL-OR-NOTHING and that partial conversion REGRESSES; the same all-or-nothing property means partial conversion is also worthless as a MEASUREMENT. RULE: before spending a probe on an address-form residual, COUNT the sites sharing the subexpression (the `--ops` opcode multiset totals do this for free - `+18 add` names both the mechanism and its population in one line), and convert the whole population or not at all. Corollary for the address-pre-hoist law: its 'no address spelling can dislodge the hoist' scope is sound where it was measured, on a hoist serving ONE site or a fixed pair, and does not extend to a multi-site population where the spelling determines whether the population exists at all.

OPERATIONAL ORDER THAT FOUND THIS, worth reusing on any standing instruction-count deficit: read the `--ops` opcode multiset BEFORE any aligned read. `target-only: +18 add +1 stw / ours-only: -1 addi -1 mr -1 stwx` sums to exactly the 16-instruction deficit and names the missing construct outright; the aligned read then only has to confirm which source statement each `add` belongs to. Three prior sessions on this function read positions and branch rows first and never counted opcodes.
